title: jev-chat/jev-chat-jarvis
why_read: A messaging co-pilot app that reads chat screens and suggests replies, of limited technical novelty and some concerning privacy implications around screen-reading tools.
analysis: This project is a mobile app that acts as a conversational co-pilot within apps like QQ, X, and Feishu, reading on-screen content to suggest candidate replies that the user can manually insert into the input field. It claims to be non-intrusive, using only read-only screen access without hooking or modifying the host apps' binaries, which somewhat limits invasiveness but still raises questions about screen-reading permissions and data handling. Technically, this is a fairly standard use of screen-reading APIs combined with an LLM backend to generate response suggestions, without much novel engineering beyond integration work. The privacy and terms-of-service implications of automated screen scraping on third-party chat apps are worth noting even though the tool keeps a human in the loop before sending.
